summary: Set 108 Session 4 of 4, set-terminal: the tutorial was WALKED and the UAT checklist cut from that walk, in that order, on Set 107's evidence that a checklist written from a document rather than from a walk documents intent, not reality. THE WALK IS PARTIAL AND SAYS SO: every command the tutorial prints was run and all three services were built and driven against each other, but the DABBLER LIFECYCLE each part routes through -- `Dabbler: New Module`, the Work Explorer, and the plan-set -> decomposition-set -> implement sequence -- WAS NOT EXECUTED; the code was written directly by the orchestrator acting as the reader's agent. The close backstop caught an earlier draft calling this 'end to end' and was right to; the claim is corrected throughout rather than defended, and this gap is now the single strongest reason the human UAT walk is still required. The spec's Step 1 required the walk's staffing to be agreed with the operator; three costed options were put and THE OPERATOR CHOSE the full A-D walk performed by the orchestrator, acting as both the reader and the AI agent the tutorial tells the reader to hand its contract sections to. THREE RULES WERE BOUND IN ADVANCE, in ai-assignment.md, so they could not be relaxed once results started arriving: CONTRACT-ONLY CONSTRUCTION (Parts A-C built from the tutorial's contract sections alone, the published answer key's source not opened until Part D); STRICT COPY-PASTE (commands run exactly as printed, a failure recorded as a document defect rather than quietly repaired -- adopted verbatim from the step-3.5 analyst's third risk); and WALKING AS `denmi`, a name appearing nowhere in a document whose examples are `priya` and `alex`, so nothing could pass by accidentally matching an example. THE HEADLINE RESULT: all four documented response bodies came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the strings the tutorial prints -- converter's 200 (379 chars), its 400 (421 chars), its unknown-schema 400, and persistence's batch 400 -- compared programmatically against the literal document lines, first run, no iteration against them. That makes the tutorial's central premise (its contract sections are sufficient to build against) falsifiable, tested, and held. Everything the document flags as easy to get wrong was in fact carried by the prose: the camelCase envelope with row keys passed through verbatim, a blank optional column arriving as an explicit null, Amount keeping its written scale, and `line` counting physical file lines with the header as line 1. 84 tests green across the three modules (29/29/26) against the answer key's 74 -- close enough to reassure, different enough to prove nothing was copied. BEYOND WHAT THE TUTORIAL CLAIMS: the document is careful that a solo Part D 'cannot prove conformance, because a single implementation always agrees with itself'. So after walking the documented solo version, the walk substituted THE PUBLISHED ANSWER KEY's converter and persistence on the 52xx band -- a genuinely independent implementation this watcher had never seen -- and drove them: batch Stored, rows read back from THEIR database, 404 for the same id on the walker's own. A bad file through their converter came back Rejected with a 400 body matching this build's on every field the contract pins. Two independent implementations honouring one contract, demonstrated rather than asserted. NEGATIVE TESTS: Part D changed ZERO code files -- re-established with a SOUND check after the close backstop correctly showed the first one was not a falsifier at all (it misses staged, committed and untracked code, and on this very repository the naive glob matched two generated obj/AssemblyInfo.cs build artifacts). The replacement pins a Part C baseline, runs `git add -A` first so untracked source cannot hide, and excludes bin/obj: 0 files, with the entire source diff for the Part D range being one appsettings.json. It was then PROVED to be a real falsifier by planting a line in DecisionTable.cs and watching it appear; the plant was reverted. The original conclusion survives the stricter test -- because it was re-run, not because the first check was adequate. watcher's suite ran 26 tests in 54 ms with both services STOPPED AND CONFIRMED DOWN by curl. The third is SPLIT after a verifier finding (below). The fourth -- two members colliding -- is not walkable solo and is recorded as unwalked, not assumed. FIVE DEFECTS FOUND, ALL FIVE FIXED (+51/-9 in three-module-pipeline.md, tutorial_gate exit 0), two of them by CUTTING an over-claim rather than adding a rule. D1 (Major): the SDK is never pinned -- `dotnet new web` produced net11.0 on a machine that satisfies the tutorial's own prerequisite check, because dotnet picks the highest SDK and this machine has an 11.0 preview, a line the tutorial PRINTS in its own example output without remarking on it; fixed with a global.json callout pointing at that very line. D2 (Major): day one's modules.yaml block opens at the `modules:` root key and omits the reader's existing module, so copying it whole silently deletes the module the same document said 500 lines earlier to leave alone; fixed with two comment lines placed INSIDE the fence, because prose beside a copyable block is what a copying reader skips. D3 (Minor): `dotnet ef` is an undocumented third prerequisite for the migrations path; documented at the point of use in Part B with the literal error text and marked conditional. D4 (Minor): the Deferred transcript promised the reader's `detail` 'will name 5101' when detail is not contractual -- promise removed. D5 (Minor): the known /run-now race was described as returning 'an empty array' when it can equally produce a 500 -- callout widened, its existing mitigation promoted from afterthought to recommendation. D1 AND D3 WERE INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED BY THE ANSWER KEY once opening it was permitted: it carries a global.json pinning 10.0.201 and a dotnet-tools.json declaring dotnet-ef 10.0.10. Both are things the reference solution needed and the tutorial never passed on -- moving them from one build's experience to a real gap. VERIFICATION: FIVE rounds, closing VERIFIED, gpt-5-6 throughout (anthropic auto-excluded). Round 1 discovery (two-way fan-out): ISSUES_FOUND, 1 blocking Major. Round 2 supplementary completeness-critic, run BEFORE any remediation: VERIFIED, ZERO new findings, so the harvest was provably complete before a fix was written. Round 3 remediation-review over the fix delta: VERIFIED, 1 fix ACCEPTED, 0 rejected, 0 new findings. ROUND 4, the close-out gate's in-process backstop (Set 084), then found TWO MORE blocking Majors that all three earlier rounds had missed -- it earned its place. Both accepted in full, neither disputed: (a) the walk was called 'end to end' while skipping the Dabbler lifecycle, and the disclosure that existed was filed under a justification that was wrong on the facts -- the MECHANICS of those commands live in adopt-dabbler.md but the INSTRUCTION to run them is in this tutorial, on its main path, in every part; (b) the Part D acceptance test was not a falsifier. Both remediated in s4-remediation-round-2.md; round 5 remediation-review closed the loop. THE FINDING WAS REAL, WAS MINE, AND WAS ACCEPTED IN FULL. s4-walk-evidence.md had marked the spec's third negative test -- 'a reader could stop cleanly after Parts A and B' -- a flat PASS on the sole basis that with all services down each suite runs alone. That does not follow: isolated unit tests prove the suites need no network, not that a reader can stop, lose context and resume. The verifier also caught the compounding half: the checklist could never have supplied the missing evidence either, since item 2 said to stop after Part A while item 3 ran Part B straight into Part C with no stop at the boundary in question. It is exactly the class the conventions block asked verifiers to hunt -- 'anywhere the evidence is narrower than the sentence describing it' -- and being caught by one's own instruction is the system working. REMEDIATED with BOTH offered fixes, because they answer different halves: (1) the missing experiment was actually RUN rather than argued about, the walk repo still being intact -- with everything stopped and confirmed DOWN, converter cold-started and Part A's finish line came back byte-identical AGAIN, and persistence cold-started with the batch stored during Part B reading back intact and still returning its ORIGINAL batchId as a duplicate, establishing the narrower falsifiable claim that no part leaves running processes or in-memory state a later part needs; (2) the HUMAN half is now marked UNVERIFIED and pushed to checklist item 3, which gained a mandatory stop ('close every terminal, close the repository, come back on a different day... do not re-read your notes when you return; use only the tutorial') with Part B timed separately. The consistency fix was propagated to ALL FOUR echoes in the same pass before re-verifying (L-065-1). THE UAT CHECKLIST: 4 items, 10,980 chars, valid JSON, derived from the acceptance criterion one item per part. Volume bar met -- 4 items against the operator's standing ~4 target, and comparable to Set 107's for a tutorial four times the size; quality expectation stated ONCE in the preamble. Its design decision: it does NOT ask the human to re-verify what the walk proved. The preamble opens with what is already settled, then names the three things ONLY a human can supply -- per-part time from a person, stalls, and the Work Explorer no human eye has seen -- and every item's ProgrammaticVerification states what Session 4 established AND explicitly what it did not. THE LIMITS ARE DECLARED, NOT GLOSSED. The per-part HUMAN timings the spec asks for DO NOT EXIST and cannot be produced by this walk: what a stopwatch measured was an AI writing three .NET services (~30 min total), which says nothing about a reader whose time goes on reading, deciding and prompting. Recorded as orchestrator wall-clock and explicitly disclaimed. The prerequisites section CANNOT BE FALSIFIED on this machine, which is the machine the tutorial was written on -- both checks passing is a non-finding, not a pass. No human has seen the Work Explorer; the day-one manifest was instead driven through the SHIPPING readModulesManifest / classifyModulesManifest / computeVisibleModules, returning four `declared` rows in manifest order with zero warnings and the reader's pre-existing module preserved. SUITE GREEN: 3143 passed, 6 skipped, 8 deselected in 32m14s -- identical counts to S3's baseline, as expected for a session that changed no Python. tutorial_gate.py exit 0 after the fixes. Layer 3 not run and L-064-12 does not arm: no Explorer-rendering surface, state writer or fixture changed. ADVISORY PATH-AWARE CRITIQUE saved with two distinct providers (gemini-2.5-pro VERIFIED 0 findings; gpt-5.4 ISSUES_FOUND 1 Major). Its finding is REAL and was verified by reading the file: adopt-dabbler.md promises host neutrality and uses 'Your host' blocks throughout -- step 7 correctly names both `gh pr create` and `az repos pr create` -- but step 8 at line 295 says 'merge the pull request on GitHub' with no ADO branch, which matters because staff are on ADO today. ADJUDICATED AS A DEFERRED RESIDUAL, not fixed and not dismissed: `git log -L 295,295` shows the line was introduced by SET 107 S2 (bf3eaee), so it is pre-existing rather than drift this set introduced; it is outside S4's declared Touches and the set's 'no estate changes' non-goal; the one precedent for an out-of-scope fix in this set (S3's tutorial_gate repair) required explicit operator approval, which was not sought here; and the owed adopt-dabbler walk -- this session's #1 next-set recommendation -- will walk exactly that step on both hosts. Handed to the operator with the one-line fix identified. STEP 9: proposes L-108-1, 'a document walk must bind its anti-flattery rules before it starts, or it confirms the document instead of testing it', with the trade it requires named -- archive L-075-1, last cited at set 084 -- and LEFT FOR OPERATOR ACCEPT/REJECT rather than applied, because both guidance files are at ceiling (project-guidance 100%, lessons-learned 99%) and a self-authored swap that displaces someone else's lesson for one this session just learned is exactly the bias not to trust. Noted against my own proposal: L-075-1 is thematically adjacent to D1/D3 and was NOT cited, because stretching a citation to protect a lesson from archival would corrupt the usage signal that drives the decision. FOLLOW-ONS: the Java track, now unblocked by the spec's own condition ('separate set, after this one is walked'); the step-3.5 analyst emitting non-existent engines and models THREE SESSIONS RUNNING (bedrock, then claude-3-opus-20240229/gpt-4o) with the diagnosis that the prompt asks for an identifier and supplies no catalogue; four unstated error envelopes in the contract sections, deliberately NOT fixed because none is on the walk and pinning them would enlarge what a reader must absorb before writing any code; the unwalked team scenario and unexercised ownership routing; and the owed adopt-dabbler.md walk, carried since Set 106 and now overdue by three sets. NO RELEASE: documents only, no version bump, no changelog entry in either package.
